sections.overview: The collared large-eye bream is an Australian western Pacific species of Gymnocranius, alongside the similarly sized congener G. frenatus.
sections.identification: It is silvery to whitish, often olive-brown above, with brown spots aligned along the scales and sometimes a dark bar through the eye. The FAO catalogue gives a maximum total length of 40 cm, commonly 35 cm.
sections.habitat: It occurs on sand or rubble beside reefs at about 8–40 m depth in its Australian western Pacific range.
sections.diet: The species feeds mainly on bottom-dwelling invertebrates.
sections.behavior: FAO describes it as generally solitary over sand or rubble areas next to reefs.
sections.reproduction: The species account consulted does not report a breeding season, clutch size, or other species-specific reproductive observations.
sections.ecology: Its benthic feeding links reef-edge sandy habitats with the small invertebrates living on or within the bottom.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports the species as Least Concern, with an IUCN assessment dated 2015.
